study: Martén-Rodríguez et al. 2015 Journal of Ecology
design: 28 insular and 26 mainland Caribbean Gesneriaceae species with field pollinator observations and breeding-system experiments

reproductive_assurance_layer.interpretation: Autonomous selfing did not increase as a universal island response; generalized pollination is a candidate alternative assurance route in pollinator-depauperate insular environments.

why_it_matters: A geographically distant Caribbean lineage reproduces the key qualitative pattern that insular pollinator constraints can be met by changing interaction architecture without a universal shift to autonomous selfing.
claim_boundary: This study does not directly estimate a causal effect of generalized architecture on reproductive success, so it is an independent partial pathway replication rather than a second full geography->architecture->function demonstration.
